title: AI for Weather Prediction for Africa (Project Umoya)
summary: Ishango's Project Umoya plans to fine-tune GraphCast and Aurora on African data; in a partner master's study, a fine-tuned small Aurora beat pretrained Aurora on past South African weather.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: In June 2025, Ishango proposed fine-tuning GraphCast and Aurora with African weather datasets, including reanalysis and station observations. The intended benefit is more locally relevant forecasting for agriculture, energy, and weather services. At that time, data acquisition and model validation were in progress. Community training and networking supported development. On 17 August 2025, the authors of an AIMS South Africa master's study done with Ishango reported that fine-tuning the small Aurora model on South African data beat both pretrained Aurora models over South Africa on 2022 data. They report that the fine-tuned model predicted almost all the considered variables better, especially for forecasts up to 48 hours, with exceptions such as specific humidity. As of 29 October 2026, Ishango reports that it supervised three master's projects with AIMS South Africa and that this research phase is complete. Ishango reports that its proof of concept is still in progress. It plans deployment as the next phase and seeks funders and partners for it.
purpose: Generate more locally relevant weather forecasts for African decision makers.

ratings.reason: More useful regional forecasts are intended; the only reported gain is a skill score on archived 2022 data in a master's study, and no forecast service is in use.
Better AI forecasts are meant to improve agricultural resilience and climate resilience, and no source reports either result.

ai_role.statement: The study authors compare the pretrained AuroraSmall with the same model after low-rank adaptation on South African data, so the reported skill gain comes from the fine-tuning. No source reports what forecasters or users did with the output.

Training and community building are distinct from operational forecasts or reduced weather losses.

AI weather models would learn from regional observations and generate forecasts.
